A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same TraqPoint study, with corresponding text, equations, figures and tables available for comparison. Neither contains an appendix; the supplementary material referenced in both versions is not included in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original TraqPoint experiments on pose estimation, localization, odometry and reconstruction, plus ablations in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including TraqPoint benchmark outcomes and component and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same architecture, frozen descriptor branch, hybrid sampling, trackability rewards and policy optimization. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use MegaDepth for training and pose evaluation, ScanNet for pose evaluation, Aachen Day-Night for localization, KITTI sequences 01–03 for odometry, and the same three ETH reconstruction scenes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 1–4 and Figure 4. This includes the same detector/descriptor baselines and SuperPoint with SuperGlue or LightGlue in the pose comparison.

E3.justification: Training budgets, image resolutions, data selection, feature counts, matching procedures and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Both specify five-image sequences, 256 sampled keypoints and 50,000 training steps per stage.

E4.justification: Table 5 and Figure 5 retain the same comparisons of sequential versus pairwise learning, reward components, backbones, sequence lengths and sampled-keypoint counts. The qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed choices, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Tables and sensitivity plots retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 1, 4 and 5 are unchanged. For example, TraqPoint's AUC@5° remains 55.8 on MegaDepth and 16.6 on ScanNet in Table 1, and its full-model AKTL remains 6.6 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and reward formulations in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Text reflow does not alter the mathematics, and neither version adds proofs or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about optimizing long-term trackability through sequence-aware reinforcement learning and composite rewards. The added code announcement does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of structural consistency, reconstruction tradeoffs, backbone effects and sequence-length sensitivity remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v4 adds a GitHub repository link in the abstract, stating that code 'will be available'; v1 provides no code location. This adds prospective access information without establishing code availability or changing the implementation details in Section 4.2.

R1.justification: The same 55 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against pairwise keypoint learning and earlier reinforcement-learning approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 updates author affiliation/contact information and a funding identifier, adds the code sentence, and changes 'keypoints form' to 'keypoints that form' in Section 4.7. The narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes small text-flow and spacing changes across pages 1–3, with localized rewrapping on page 8. All five figures and five tables retain their graphics, structure and captions.

improvement.justification: The method, experimental evidence, mathematical reasoning and scientific explanations are unchanged. The prospective code link adds convenience, while the other edits are small editorial or administrative updates. Because v4 still only promises code availability, these changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement.
